program.section_heading: FLORAL DESIGN AND MANAGEMENT Certificate of Achievement (STATE CODE 21800)
outcomes: Using the elements and principles of floral design and basic color theory as well as industry standards, create basic floral arrangements and corsages.
Identify by common and botanical names numerous flower and foliage varieties and determine the post-harvest care and handling procedures.
Create industry-standard floral designs for categories of special events, such as wedding décor, sympathy tributes, window displays, permanent botanicals, and event designs.
Apply business concepts to the management of a floral business, including issues related to accounting, marketing, and general management.

notes: Catalog prints ACCTG 001, BUS 005 and MGMT 013 with leading zeros; these match closed-list ACCTG 1, BUS 5 and MGMT 13 and are not treated as catalog additions.

Catalog notes 'Other courses may be substituted with prior approval of the Department Chair.'

Program description says the student 'is qualified to be employed in a flower shop'; this names a workplace rather than a job title, so no career was recorded. Careers are otherwise referred to the Gainful Employment Disclosure website.
